definitions.gloss: senior Shinto priest; shrine priest (second rank)
definitions.explanation: A Shinto priesthood rank, second in the hierarchy below the chief priest. Responsible for assisting in shrine rituals and administration.

examples.japanese: {禰宜|ねぎ}が{祝詞|のりと}を{奏上|そうじょう}した。
examples.english: The shrine priest recited a Shinto prayer.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{地元|じもと}の{神社|じんじゃ}で{禰宜|ねぎ}を{務|つと}めている。
examples.english: He serves as a senior priest at the local shrine.

examples.japanese: {禰宜|ねぎ}は{宮司|ぐうじ}を{補佐|ほさ}し、{日々|ひび}の{祭祀|さいし}や{神社|じんじゃ}の{運営|うんえい}に{携|たずさ}わる{重要|じゅうよう}な{役職|やくしょく}だ。
examples.english: The negi is an important position that assists the chief priest and is involved in daily rituals and shrine management.

notes:
An ancient Shinto term. The word originally comes from {労|ねぎら}う (to console/comfort), reflecting the priest's role as an intermediary who comforts and serves the gods.

The Shinto priest hierarchy at most shrines is:
- {宮司|ぐうじ}: chief priest (head of the shrine)
- {禰宜|ねぎ}: senior priest (second rank)
- {権禰宜|ごんねぎ}: assistant priest (third rank)

Small shrines may have only a {宮司|ぐうじ} and no {禰宜|ねぎ}, while large shrines like Ise Jingu may have many priests at each level. The word is also a common Japanese surname.

Not to be confused with the homophone {葱|ねぎ} (green onion).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {禰宜|ねぎ}を{務|つと}める: to serve as a negi
- {権禰宜|ごんねぎ}: assistant priest
- {禰宜|ねぎ}の{装束|しょうぞく}: priest's ceremonial garments

RELATED WORDS:
- {宮司|ぐうじ}: chief priest of a Shinto shrine
- {神主|かんぬし}: Shinto priest (general term)
- {巫女|みこ}: shrine maiden
